newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen's B share market sees rapid expansion.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen's B share market sees rapid expansion.

text.p: The Shenzhen government's market revitalisation measures have succeeded in doubling the size of the city's B share market over the past 15 months, said a report in the official press.

The market in Shenzhen for class B stock, which is quoted in Hong Kong dollars, has also improved in terms of quality, with an increasing number of firms with solid profit records being listed, said the Securities Times, which is published by the Shenzhen bourse.

The market officially opened in February of 1992 with the listing of China Southern Glass Holdings Co Ltd and underwent a period of rapid development in its first year of operation, said the newspaper.
Weak profits reported by listed firms, a lack of transparency and problems involving illiquidity and an incomplete legal framework for trading later triggered plummeting share prices.

The class B market began to see a turnaround in June of last year, when the city government introduced a series of confidence-boosting policies. Those measures included simplifying trading procedures, lowering related fees and listing firms based outside of Shenzhen.
The Guangdong and Shenzhen goverments have since outlined a range of preferential policies in the areas of tax, credit and trade to foster the expansion of the province's strongest companies.
The paper said that of 40 firms with a combined 2.71 billion B shares currently listed in Shenzhen, 16 companies have floated 1.46 billion B shares since June of 1995.
Most B share firms listed in the past 15 months have more extensive listed share capital than their predecessors, with six companies each floating at least 100 million B shares, the paper said.
The newspaper said the Shenzhen B share market has also become more diverse in terms of the geographical base and scope of operations of listed firms.

While Guangdong-based firms overwhelmingly dominated the south China exchange for the first three years of its operations, companies headquartered outside the province are beginning to step up their presence in Shenzhen.
It said that there are now 12 B share firms based in other areas of the country that have floated shares in Shenzhen.
The same newspaper said in a separate article that 1996 has marked the most rapid period of expansion of Shenzhen's A share market in its five-and-a-half-year history.

It said that 42 firms issued and listed class A shares in Shenzhen in the January-August period of this year, and added that the offers raised nearly five billion yuan in combined proceeds. The newspaper added that the exchange's total turnover reached more than 400 billion yuan in the period, but it did not provide comparative figures from the previous year.
By the end of August, Shenzhen had more than seven million registered stock investors, up from 5.5 million at the beginning of the year, it said.
